clinician.final_diagnosis: Multiple myeloma (IgG kappa) and Evan's syndrome (warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia with immune thrombocytopenia)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old man presented with 2 months of fatigue, dizziness, and acute renal failure (creatinine 330 µmol/l, clearance 14 ml/min). Physical examination revealed conjunctival jaundice. Laboratory studies demonstrated Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia (hemoglobin 86 g/L, reticulocytes 5.2%, LDH 451 UI/L, indirect bilirubin 49 mmol/L, positive Direct Coombs test with warm IgG autoantibody) and severe thrombocytopenia (36×10^9/L), establishing Evan's syndrome. Workup for acute renal failure revealed IgG kappa multiple myeloma: serum protein electrophoresis showed total protein 113 g/L with M-spike 69 g/L, urine M protein 2 g/day, bone marrow aspiration showed 78% plasma cell infiltration, and whole-body CT demonstrated osteolytic lesions at C5, D4, L3, L4 vertebral bodies and left iliac wing. Treatment was initiated with bortezomib-thalidomide-dexamethasone (BTD) and continuous corticosteroids. Despite therapy, the patient experienced clinical deterioration with worsening hematologic and renal status, developed hemorrhagic manifestations (ecchymosis, hematemesis), and died secondary to lactic acidosis.
